findings.title: Faithful work and divinely made affection as a social bond
findings.claim: Within the promise that al-Rahman will make affection for those who believe and do good, the wider connections let that affection read as a public bond given by God: believers' love is set beside rival-god attachment, and divine making is shown joining estranged people.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers are the believing group, their deliberate good works, the future making verb with its beneficiaries, and wuddan. The exact target of 2:165 juxtaposes love of rivals with believers' greater love for Allah; 5:2 makes righteousness cooperative practice; 60:7 places divine making beside affection between former enemies; 8:63 depicts God joining hostile hearts beyond material means; and 71:23 names Wadd among idols. Those contacts meet the focus words and its make-for-them relation, shifting wudd from an affection that could be pictured only inwardly to a publicly established bond, while the common-noun affection reading remains intact.
findings.reader_payoff: The promised affection can be pictured as a shared bond that divine action establishes and that can repair distance; the Wadd echo also gives the promise a concrete counter-image to cultic attachment.
findings.containment: 19:96 names the beneficiaries and the affection but does not identify them as former enemies, name a particular idol, or state that it alludes to the wider passages. The Wadd contact is a root-level analogy: wuddan remains the common noun for affection in the focus, not the idol's proper name.

epistemic.reason: The cross-run support anchors five exact focus words and the wider connection targets supply exact Arabic. Their notes remain nominations, target morphology is not supplied, and the reconciliation and Wadd extensions are analogical, so the global contact is qualified rather than a direct-allusion claim.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Temel cekirdek bir haberin, sozun veya hakikatin dogru sayilmasidir.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus's plural believing form carries the branch's sense of affirming what is true.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 2:165 sets believers' stronger love for Allah beside the love of rival gods.
branch_activations.activation: Because the focus leaves the object of belief unstated, this wider contrast gives the verb a setting of faith amid competing attachments and links that faith to the affection promised later in the clause.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The beneficiaries appear as a group whose affirmation is relationally oriented toward Allah, so the gift of wudd belongs beside their faith and good works.
branch_activations.boundary: The wider verse supplies a parallel setting, not a grammatical object for 19:96 and not proof of a direct citation.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: birini veya şeyi belirli bir duruma getirme
branch_activations.facet_statement: Var olan bir katılımcının durumunu, niteliğini veya konumunu değiştiren ettirici işlemi bildirir.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus's future making verb carries a state-changing operation, with wuddan as its object and lahum as its beneficiary relation.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 60:7 describes Allah making affection between people who had been hostile to one another.
branch_activations.activation: The repeated making-and-affection relation supplies a social instance of the focus verb's state-changing use; joined to its plural beneficiaries, the focus's promise becomes an established relation among people.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Wudd appears as affection placed into the beneficiaries' social world, not only as a private feeling or an abstract reward.
branch_activations.boundary: 19:96 does not identify its beneficiaries as former enemies; 60:7 is a wider parallel, not the same event.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Kişi, iş veya şey bozukluğun ve kötülüğün karşıtı olan iyi, düzgün ve yararlı bir durumda bulunur.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus's definite plural salihat names the recognized category of sound and good deeds.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 5:2 calls believers to cooperate in righteousness and piety and sets that cooperation against wrongdoing and aggression.
branch_activations.activation: The wider command gives the focus's good-deed category a shared ethical setting, so the affection promised for its practitioners can be read alongside collective upright conduct.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The condition for the promised wudd includes good action as a social practice, not merely as a private quality.
branch_activations.boundary: The focus does not specify the particular cooperative deeds named in 5:2 or make every righteous deed collective.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir yapanın bilerek ortaya koyduğu iş veya eylem anlamı çekirdektir.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus's completed plural verb names deliberate doing and takes righteous deeds as its explicit object.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 5:2 describes believers cooperating in good conduct as a shared act.
branch_activations.activation: That wider collective practice meets the focus's plural doing and its good-deed object, making the action that defines the beneficiaries legible as capable of communal form.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Faithful action can be heard as work enacted among people as well as individual deeds.
branch_activations.boundary: The focus does not prescribe 5:2's specific cooperative acts; the connection broadens the social picture without replacing its general wording.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir kişiye ya da şeye sevgi beslemek ve ona gönülden yakınlık duymak.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus's indefinite accusative wuddan names affection directed to the beneficiaries.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 60:7 depicts Allah placing affection between former enemies, while 8:63 says God joined hostile hearts beyond what spending could accomplish.
branch_activations.activation: Both wider scenes give affection a public, relational shape; their divine agency meets the focus's making verb and love object, so wudd is perceived as a bond that can cross hostility and hold people together.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The affection promised in 19:96 can be read as God-given social cohesion as well as loving closeness.
branch_activations.boundary: The focus does not state that its beneficiaries were formerly hostile or reproduce either wider scene.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Birbirinden uzaklaşmış veya çatışmış insanlar arasındaki olumsuz ilişki giderilir.
branch_activations.carrier: Salihat names good deeds in the focus and carries the same supplied root as the branch of reconciliation between people.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 8:63 describes God joining hearts that human spending could not unite.
branch_activations.activation: The focus's good-deed carrier meets this concrete scene of restored relation, while its wudd object names affection for a group; together they let good action resonate with social repair.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The good works associated with the promised affection can carry a repair-oriented social possibility alongside their ordinary righteous-deed sense.
branch_activations.boundary: 19:96 does not specify peacemaking deeds or use salihat to name reconciliation in this clause; this is a root-level analogy to the wider scene.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Biçimin tapınılan belirli bir puta verilen özel ad olarak kullanılması.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus's common noun wuddan carries the supplied w-d-d root; its ordinary meaning here remains affection.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 71:23 includes Wadd in a list of named objects of worship.
branch_activations.activation: The named idol in the wider verse meets the focus noun through their shared root and surface echo; beside the focus's divinely given affection, it supplies the candidate's false-god contrast with a concrete cultic counterpart.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The promised affection can be heard against an idol-name from the same root, sharpening the difference between a bond given by God and attachment to a cultic patron.
branch_activations.boundary: The focus's syntax makes wuddan a common noun for affection, not the idol's proper name; the echo does not establish identity or direct allusion.
